summary: Added Custom Theme tools for Tableau Studio: inspect and export a theme, then apply it to the open workbook with Preserve conflict handling, plus a Publish Workbook dialog launcher.
Added live datasource refresh and extract refresh, and a search over fields and calculations in the live open workbook that reports Rows, Columns, and Marks placements.

Added formatting and composition tools: set rounded corners on dashboard zones, set mark labels and number formats across up to 12 worksheets at once, and compose the ordered points of an existing story.

Parameters now apply in place without reopening the session. Workbook datasource listings include type and extract flags, and Get App Info reports live Start Page, Data Source page, and presentation-mode state.

Added datasource apply and inspect tools, plus Dialogs and Tableau Agent groups: replace a datasource document in the open workbook, read datasource metadata or XML, list and invoke Studio dialogs, refresh automatic updates, and show or hide the Start Page.
Added Desktop Tools — a new family of 57 tools for authoring directly in Tableau Studio, spanning 12 groups including Binder, Dashboards, Worksheets, and Data Sources.

Expanded sheet lifecycle and workbook I/O: add, rename, and delete worksheets, dashboards, and storyboards; open, save, and export the workbook; pause and resume automatic updates; and read a worksheet's underlying data.
Updated the Web Tools documentation and split the tool reference into dedicated Web Tools and Desktop Tools home pages, each with an auto-updating, filterable tool catalog.
Added inline availability notes so every tool page shows the release it first became available.
General availability of Tableau MCP — 32 tools for exploring and managing published Tableau content, spanning 13 groups including Data Q&A, Pulse, Workbooks, Views, and Admin Insights.
Introduced the Web Tools reference: a page per tool documenting its arguments, results, and the Tableau APIs it calls, with a filterable tool catalog.
